audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel chapter 23, first-pass draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for last-words genre, Spirit speech, just-rule standard, covenant confidence, thorn-burning rhetoric, warrior lists and variants, mass-killing boasts, land and food defense, dangerous leader desire, water poured as blood, foreign and regional identities, animal violence, and Uriah's final placement.

verses.restored: These are last words of David: declaration of David son of Jesse, declaration of man raised on high, anointed of Divine of Jacob, pleasant singer of songs of Israel.

familiar.text: Now these be the last words of David. David the son of Jesse said, and the man who was raised up on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel, said,

modern.text: These are the last words of David: “The oracle of David son of Jesse, the oracle of the man raised on high, the one anointed by the God of Jacob, and the sweet psalmist of Israel:

original.text: וְאֵ֛לֶּה דִּבְרֵ֥י דָוִ֖ד הָאַֽחֲרֹנִ֑ים נְאֻ֧ם דָּוִ֣ד בֶּן יִשַׁ֗י וּנְאֻ֤ם הַגֶּ֨בֶר֙ הֻ֣קַם עָ֔ל מְשִׁ֨יחַ֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וּנְעִ֖ים זְמִר֥וֹת יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Spirit of YHWH spoke through me, and YHWH's word was upon my tongue.

familiar.text: The Spirit of the LORD spake by me, and his word was in my tongue.

modern.text: The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me; His word was on my tongue.

original.text: ר֥וּחַ יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֶּר בִּ֑י וּמִלָּת֖וֹ עַל לְשׁוֹנִֽי

verses.restored: Divine of Israel said; Rock of Israel spoke to me: One ruling over humanity with justice, ruling in fear of Divine,

familiar.text: The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spake to me, He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God.

modern.text: The God of Israel spoke; the Rock of Israel said to me, ‘He who rules the people with justice, who rules in the fear of God,

original.text: אָמַר֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לִ֥י דִבֶּ֖ר צ֣וּר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מוֹשֵׁל֙ בָּאָדָ֔ם צַדִּ֕יק מוֹשֵׁ֖ל יִרְאַ֥ת אֱלֹהִֽים

verses.restored: is like light of morning when sun rises, morning without clouds, when from brightness after rain grass springs from earth.

familiar.text: And he shall be as the light of the morning, when the sun riseth, even a morning without clouds; as the tender grass springing out of the earth by clear shining after rain.

modern.text: is like the light of the morning at sunrise of a cloudless dawn, the glistening after the rain on the sprouting grass of the earth.’

original.text: וּכְא֥וֹר בֹּ֖קֶר יִזְרַח שָׁ֑מֶשׁ בֹּ֚קֶר לֹ֣א עָב֔וֹת מִנֹּ֥גַהּ מִמָּטָ֖ר דֶּ֥שֶׁא מֵאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: Is not my house thus with Divine? For an everlasting covenant YHWH set for me, ordered in all and guarded. For all my rescue and every desire—will YHWH not cause it to grow?

familiar.text: Although my house be not so with God; yet he hath made with me an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things, and sure: for this is all my salvation, and all my desire, although he make it not to grow.

modern.text: Is not my house right with God? For He has established with me an everlasting covenant, ordered and secured in every part. Will He not bring about my full salvation and my every desire?

original.text: כִּֽי לֹא כֵ֥ן בֵּיתִ֖י עִם אֵ֑ל כִּי֩ בְרִ֨ית עוֹלָ֜ם שָׂ֣ם לִ֗י עֲרוּכָ֤ה בַכֹּל֙ וּשְׁמֻרָ֔ה כִּֽי כָל יִשְׁעִ֥י וְכָל חֵ֖פֶץ כִּֽי לֹ֥א יַצְמִֽיחַ

verses.restored: But worthless ones are all like thorns thrust away, because they cannot be taken by hand.

familiar.text: But the sons of Belial shall be all of them as thorns thrust away, because they cannot be taken with hands:

modern.text: But the worthless are all like thorns raked aside, for they can never be gathered by hand.

original.text: וּבְלִיַּ֕עַל כְּק֥וֹץ מֻנָ֖ד כֻּלָּ֑הַם כִּֽי לֹ֥א בְיָ֖ד יִקָּֽחוּ

verses.restored: One who touches them arms oneself with iron and shaft of spear, and they are utterly burned with fire where they lie.

familiar.text: But the man that shall touch them must be fenced with iron and the staff of a spear; and they shall be utterly burned with fire in the same place.

modern.text: The man who touches them must be armed with iron or with the shaft of a spear. The fire burns them to ashes in the place where they lie.” David’s Mighty Men (1 Chronicles 11:10–47)

verses.restored: These are names of mighty warriors of David: Josheb-basshebeth the Tahchemonite, chief of Three; he wielded his spear against eight hundred slain at one time.

familiar.text: These be the names of the mighty men whom David had: The Tachmonite that sat in the seat, chief among the captains; the same was Adino the Eznite: he lift up his spear against eight hundred, whom he slew at one time.

modern.text: These are the names of David’s mighty men: Josheb-basshebeth the Tahchemonite was chief of the Three. He wielded his spear against eight hundred men, whom he killed at one time.

familiar.text: And after him was Eleazar the son of Dodo the Ahohite, one of the three mighty men with David, when they defied the Philistines that were there gathered together to battle, and the men of Israel were gone away:

modern.text: Next in command was Eleazar son of Dodo the Ahohite. As one of the three mighty men, he went with David to taunt the Philistines who had gathered for battle at Pas-dammim. The men of Israel retreated,

verses.restored: He arose and struck Philistines until his hand was weary and his hand clung to sword. YHWH made a great rescue that day, and people returned after him only to strip spoil.

familiar.text: He arose, and smote the Philistines until his hand was weary, and his hand clave unto the sword: and the LORD wrought a great victory that day; and the people returned after him only to spoil.

modern.text: but Eleazar stood his ground and struck the Philistines until his hand grew weary and stuck to his sword. The LORD brought about a great victory that day. Then the troops returned to him, but only to plunder the dead.

original.text: ה֣וּא קָם֩ וַיַּ֨ךְ בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֜ים עַ֣ד כִּֽי יָגְעָ֣ה יָד֗וֹ וַתִּדְבַּ֤ק יָדוֹ֙ אֶל הַחֶ֔רֶב וַיַּ֧עַשׂ יְהוָ֛ה תְּשׁוּעָ֥ה גְדוֹלָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְהָעָ֛ם יָשֻׁ֥בוּ אַחֲרָ֖יו אַךְ לְפַשֵּֽׁט

verses.restored: After him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. Philistines gathered into a troop where there was a portion of field full of lentils, and people fled before Philistines.

familiar.text: And after him was Shammah the son of Agee the Hararite. And the Philistines were gathered together into a troop, where was a piece of ground full of lentiles: and the people fled from the Philistines.

modern.text: And after him was Shammah son of Agee the Hararite. When the Philistines had banded together near a field full of lentils, Israel’s troops fled from them.

familiar.text: But he stood in the midst of the ground, and defended it, and slew the Philistines: and the LORD wrought a great victory.

modern.text: But Shammah took his stand in the middle of the field, defended it, and struck down the Philistines. So the LORD brought about a great victory.

modern.text: At harvest time, three of the thirty chief men went down to David at the cave of Adullam, while a company of Philistines was encamped in the Valley of Rephaim.

modern.text: At that time David was in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines was at Bethlehem.

modern.text: David longed for water and said, “Oh, that someone would get me a drink of water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem!”

familiar.text: And the three mighty men brake through the host of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem, that was by the gate, and took it, and brought it to David: nevertheless he would not drink thereof, but poured it out unto the LORD.

modern.text: So the three mighty men broke through the Philistine camp, drew water from the well near the gate of Bethlehem, and brought it back to David. But he refused to drink it; instead, he poured it out to the LORD,

verses.restored: He said, Far be it from me, YHWH, that I should do this. Is this not blood of men who went at risk of their lives? He was not willing to drink it. These things three mighty warriors did.

familiar.text: And he said, Be it far from me, O LORD, that I should do this: is not this the blood of the men that went in jeopardy of their lives? therefore he would not drink it. These things did these three mighty men.

modern.text: saying, “Far be it from me, O LORD, to do this! Is this not the blood of the men who risked their lives?” So he refused to drink it. Such were the exploits of the three mighty men.

modern.text: Now Abishai, the brother of Joab and son of Zeruiah, was chief of the Three, and he lifted his spear against three hundred men, killed them, and won a name along with the Three.

modern.text: And Benaiah son of Jehoiada was a man of valor from Kabzeel, a man of many exploits. He struck down two champions of Moab, and on a snowy day he went down into a pit and killed a lion.

modern.text: He also killed an Egyptian, a huge man. Although the Egyptian had a spear in his hand, Benaiah went against him with a club, snatched the spear from his hand, and killed the Egyptian with his own spear.

translation_notes: The 'last words' are a literary and theological collection, not necessarily David's final chronological speech.
The standard in verses 3-4 is justice under reverence for Divine. It judges David's reign; David's anointing does not prove he fulfilled it.
The everlasting covenant expresses royal confidence but cannot provide hereditary immunity, theocracy, supersessionism, or modern territorial entitlement.
The thorn-burning image dehumanizes opponents as disposable vegetation. It may not support execution, hell threats, political purges, or violence against people labeled worthless.
Warrior accounts preserve courage and community memory while also boasting hundreds of deaths. Casualty totals are not a holiness metric.
Eleazar's hand clinging to sword may reflect extreme exertion or injury. Trauma and bodily cost remain beneath the heroic summary.
Shammah's defense of a lentil field protects food and land, but the story still rests on killing combatants.

David's longing for Bethlehem water sends three people through lethal danger. His later refusal to drink recognizes their risk, but leaders are responsible for desires subordinates may interpret as commands.
Pouring the water as 'blood' refuses consumption of sacrifice offered for royal appetite; it does not erase the dangerous mission.
The list includes people from Judah, Benjamin, Ammon, Zobah, Gad, Beeroth, and other communities. Foreign identity does not reduce loyalty or humanity.
Benaiah's animal and human killings are reputation stories, not instructions for masculinity, animal cruelty, or ethnic superiority.
Uriah the Hittite closes the list. His name exposes the contradiction between David's celebrated warriors and the king who arranged one warrior's death.
safety_note: Do not turn the mighty-warrior catalogue into a masculinity test, weapon fantasy, or claim that high body counts prove Divine favor. Measure royal greatness by justice, protection of life, and accountability. Let Uriah's final name challenge every heroic summary that would forget the people power consumed.
